Dockerfile.text:
FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY flow.mjs page.mjs stripe.mjs server.mjs ./
RUN mkdir -p /data && chown node /data
USER node
ENV PORT=8080 STATE=/tmp/state.json
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK CMD wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz || exit 1
CMD ["node", "server.mjs"]

README.md.text:
# cancel-flow

After using this, you can now **put a smart exit flow between "Cancel
subscription" and Stripe, on your own server**: it asks why, offers the save
that fits the answer, cancels cleanly if the customer still wants out, and
tells you which reasons you are actually winning. That used to mean paying a
retention service a monthly fee that grows with your revenue and handing it
your customer list.

**Live tool:** https://duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects/cancel-flow/

Two parts, both free and MIT:

- **`index.html`** — the customer's view of the flow for any reason, plan price
  and offer settings, plus a revenue estimate from your own numbers. Runs in the
  browser; nothing is uploaded.
- **`server.mjs`** — the service. One Node process, **zero dependencies**, state
  in one JSON file. It serves the hosted cancel page, applies the save offer or
  the cancellation in Stripe, and reports at `/v1/summary`.

## Why someone would use this

| Today | Cost / catch | Cancel Flow |
|---|---|---|
| Stripe customer portal cancellation survey + one retention coupon | Free, but one offer for every reason and little reporting | A different offer per reason, a cooldown, per-reason save rate |
| Churnkey, ProfitWell Retain, Brightback and similar | Paid, usually scaled to your MRR; your customers' data goes to a third party | Runs in your account, no fee, nobody else sees your customers |
| A flow you build yourself | Easy to get wrong: double discounts, canceling the wrong subscription, offers on trials | Signed links, ownership check, idempotent writes, cooldown, dry-run default |

Honest limits: the results dashboard is a single page on your own server (no accounts, no
history beyond the state file), and win-back emails are
plain-text only (off until you set `WINBACK_URL`). It does not claim a save rate; measure it on your own data.
If the Stripe portal's built-in survey already works for you, keep it.

## What it does

1. **Signed one-time-per-subscription links.** Your app calls
   `POST /v1/links {"subscription":"sub_..."}` (admin key) when a signed-in
   customer clicks Cancel and redirects them to the returned URL. The link
   expires (default 60 min) and the server checks with Stripe that the
   subscription belongs to the customer named in the link before changing
   anything.
2. **Asks why** (seven reasons that map to Stripe's `cancellation_details.feedback`
   values) and an optional comment.
3. **Offers the fit** (`flow.mjs`, overridable with `POLICY_JSON`):

   | Reason | Default offer |
   |---|---|
   | too expensive | 30% off for 3 months (annual plans: 30% off the next renewal only) |
   | switching to another product | 20% off for 3 months |
   | not using it enough / only need a break | pause billing 2 / 3 months (`pause_collection`, resumes on its own) |
   | something is not working | link to support, then cancel is still one click |
   | missing a feature / other | no offer; straight to cancel (you read the comment) |

   No discount to trialing customers; **one accepted save per customer per 365
   days** so nobody farms coupons; clamps (100% max, 12 months max) so a typo
   cannot give the product away.
4. **Cancels at period end** with the reason and comment attached to the
   subscription in Stripe. The customer keeps access until the date shown.
5. **Is replay-safe.** Each session ends once; Stripe writes carry idempotency
   keys; the webhook is de-duplicated; reloading the page does not start a second
   session.
6. **Wins back, if you turn it on.** Set `WINBACK_URL` (your pricing or
   sign-up page) and customers who cancelled through the flow get up to two
   plain-text emails after their subscription actually ends (default 14 and 60
   days), worded for the reason they gave. Each step is sent once; nothing goes
   to anyone who opted out or has already subscribed again; every email has a
   one-click unsubscribe (also as the `List-Unsubscribe` header) and your postal
   address (`COMPANY_ADDRESS`, which the law in many places requires). The
   second email can carry a code you create in Stripe (`WINBACK_CODE`). Dry-run
   logs what it would send. `/v1/summary` adds emailed, opted out and
   resubscribed. It claims no win-back rate; it counts yours.
7. **A/B tests offers.** Add `experiments` to `POLICY_JSON`, for example
   `{"experiments":{"too_expensive":{"variants":{"B":{"type":"discount","percent":15,"months":6}}}}}`.
   The offer in `offers` stays the control (arm A); customers are split evenly by a
   hash of customer and reason, so one customer always sees the same arm.
   `/v1/summary` then reports `experiments`: offers, saves, save rate and monthly
   revenue kept per arm, a two-sided two-proportion p-value, and a verdict that stays
   "keep collecting" until both arms have 30 offers and p < 0.05. Small shops will
   wait a long time for 30 per arm; treat early gaps as noise.
8. **Shows results at `/admin`.** Open `https://<your host>/admin`, paste `ADMIN_KEY`, and see
   save rate by reason, offer tests, win-back and recent sessions, plus a CSV export. The page holds
   no data and no key; the key stays in the tab and goes only to your server.
9. **Reports** `GET /v1/summary` (started, offered, saved, save rate, by reason,
   monthly revenue kept by discounts) and `GET /v1/sessions` (admin key).

## Run it

```sh
cd ventures/cancel-flow
node --test        # 53 tests, no network
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=rk_test_... STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_... \
ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) LINK_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 16) \
PUBLIC_URL=https://cancel.example.com COMPANY_NAME=Acme node server.mjs
```

It starts in **DRY_RUN** (the default): the whole flow works and is recorded, the
page shows a "test mode" banner, and no subscription is changed. Walk through it
with a **test-mode** subscription, then set `DRY_RUN=false`.

Setup in Stripe:

1. Restricted key: Subscriptions write, Coupons write, Customers read.
2. Webhook endpoint `https://<host>/webhook/stripe` for
   `customer.subscription.deleted` (records true churn) and, for win-back,
   `customer.subscription.created`. Win-back also needs Customers read.
3. In your app, make the Cancel button call `/v1/links` server-side and redirect.
   The admin key must never reach the browser.

| Env | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | required |
| `ADMIN_KEY` | bearer token for `/v1/*` |
| `LINK_SECRET` | signs the customer links |
| `PUBLIC_URL` | where this server is reachable (links are built from it) |
| `COMPANY_NAME`, `BRAND_COLOR`, `RETURN_URL` | page wording, `#rrggbb` accent, https "back to app" link |
| `POLICY_JSON` | override offers, e.g. `{"offers":{"too_expensive":{"type":"discount","percent":20,"months":2}},"cooldownDays":180,"supportUrl":"https://example.com/help"}` |
| `FRAME_ANCESTORS` | allow embedding the page in an iframe, e.g. `https://app.example.com` (default none) |
| `STATE` | path of the JSON state file |
| `WINBACK_URL` | turns win-back emails on; where the email sends people (https) |
| `RESEND_API_KEY`, `MAIL_FROM`, `COMPANY_ADDRESS` | needed to send win-back for real (`DRY_RUN=false`) |
| `WINBACK_CODE`, `WINBACK_CODE_TEXT` | optional code mentioned in the last email |
| `WINBACK_JSON` | e.g. `{"steps":[{"afterDays":7},{"afterDays":30}],"maxPerRun":25}` (1 to 4 steps, 1 to 365 days) |

Mint a link from your backend (any language, it is one HTTP call):

```sh
curl -s -X POST "$PUBLIC_URL/v1/links" -H "authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" \
  -d '{"subscription":"sub_123","ttlMinutes":30}'
```

## One-click deploy (your own account)

Fork this repository and open `https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>`.
`render.yaml` builds the `Dockerfile` here in **your** Render account with a 1 GB
disk for the state file and generated `ADMIN_KEY` and `LINK_SECRET`. Nothing runs
on the author's side. Docker anywhere works too:
`docker build -t cancel-flow . && docker run -p 8080:8080 -v cf:/data -e STATE=/data/state.json ... cancel-flow`.

## Status and what is not verified

Everything in `node --test` passes against a fake Stripe. It has **not** been run
against live Stripe by the author: do that in test mode before going live.
Cancellation rules differ by country and state (some require cancelling to be as
easy as signing up); you are the operator. Keep a plain cancel path, and do not
make the offer step mandatory beyond one screen.

Files: `flow.mjs` (decisions, summary; also runs in the browser), `page.mjs` (hosted
page), `admin.mjs` (results dashboard), `winback.mjs` (win-back emails), `stripe.mjs` (webhook verification, API calls), `server.mjs` (HTTP shell),
`index.html` (simulator). Sibling venture for failed payments: `../dunning-engine`.

Support the project: <https://github.com/sponsors/Duncan-Haywood>.

## Other self-deploy paths

`docker-compose.yml` runs it on any box with Docker (the command is at its top). Fly.io: the steps are at the top of `fly.toml`. Both keep state on a volume and run in your own account.

VENTURE.yaml.text:
name: cancel-flow
description: >-
  Self-hosted Stripe cancellation flow: asks why the customer is leaving, offers
  the save that fits the reason (pause for the busy, discount for the
  price-sensitive, a human for the stuck), cancels at period end if they still
  want out, and reports save rate by reason. Browser simulator plus a
  zero-dependency server with a one-click Render deploy.
stage: prototype
owner: duncan

# Screened 2026-10-15. Paid market is real and proven: Churnkey, ProfitWell
# Retain (Paddle), Brightback (Chargebee), Baremetrics Cancellation Insights and
# Churn Buster sell cancellation flows and save offers to subscription
# businesses, typically as a monthly fee that rises with MRR. Stripe's customer
# portal has a built-in cancellation survey and one retention coupon: the free
# baseline. The gap: indie and small SaaS teams who want a different offer per
# reason, a discount-farming cooldown and the answers in a store they own, and
# who will not hand customer data to a third party or pay for the volume.
# duplicate_check.py top score 0.18 (stripe-churn-cohort-analyzer reads past
# churn from a CSV; this is the live exit flow). Sibling of dunning-engine
# (involuntary churn); this is voluntary churn, same buyer, same Stripe pieces.
#
# First visitor: indie SaaS founders on Indie Hackers, r/SaaS, r/stripe and Hacker
# News asking "churnkey alternative", "cancellation survey stripe", "save offer
# when customer cancels", "reduce voluntary churn". Volume not measured with an
# external tool.
#
# Path to revenue (payments stay off): free and MIT as the lead magnet; a hosted
# version, done-for-you setup or GitHub Sponsors are the paid steps -- hosting
# under the public name and billing are owner-gated.

hypotheses:
  - claim: >-
      Indie SaaS founders will deploy a dry-run cancellation flow in their own
      account once the simulator shows them a reason-specific offer, because
      Stripe's portal gives one coupon for every reason and the paid tools bill
      by MRR.
    status: untested
    checked: null
    evidence: customer-contact
  - claim: >-
      Matching the offer to the stated reason (pause for "not using", discount for
      "too expensive", none for "missing feature") keeps more subscribers than one
      blanket coupon for the same merchant, and the per-reason report is what makes
      owners keep the flow switched on.
    status: untested
    checked: null
    evidence: customer-contact

economics:
  currency: USD
  mrr: null
  monthly_cost: 0
  customers: null

budget:
  monthly_cap: 1
  protected: false

kill_criteria:
  - Fewer than three distinct GitHub users (issues, stars, or a pasted report) engage within 90 days of the page being reachable from the published site.
  - A user reports a customer discounted twice, a subscription changed without the customer's click, or a cancel that did not take effect; the idempotency, cooldown and signed-link paths come before any new feature.

links:
  production: https://duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects/cancel-flow/
  analytics: null

fly.toml.text:
# Fly.io self-deploy, in your own account (needs flyctl and a card on file with Fly):
#   fly launch --copy-config --no-deploy --dockerfile Dockerfile
#   fly volumes create state --size 1
#   fly secrets set ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) LINK_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
#   (optional settings from render.yaml, e.g. PUBLIC_URL, go in with `fly secrets set` too)
#   fly deploy
# One machine that never auto-stops: the state file lives on its volume.
app = "cancel-flow-CHANGE-ME"
primary_region = "iad"

[build]
  dockerfile = "Dockerfile"

[env]
  PORT = "8080"
  STATE = "/data/state.json"
  DRY_RUN = "true"

[mounts]
  source = "state"
  destination = "/data"

[http_service]
  internal_port = 8080
  force_https = true
  auto_stop_machines = "off"
  auto_start_machines = false
  min_machines_running = 1
  [[http_service.checks]]
    path = "/healthz"
    interval = "30s"
    timeout = "5s"

index.html.text:
Ask why they are leaving, then offer the one thing that might keep them

Someone who cancels because the price stings needs a different answer than someone who has not opened the product in a month. Cancel Flow puts a short exit survey between your "Cancel subscription" button and Stripe, offers a discount, a pause, or a human matched to the reason, cancels cleanly at period end if they still want out, and shows you the save rate for each reason. Try the customer's view below, then run the open-source server with your own Stripe key. No account with us, no monthly fee.

What your customer would see

Decision:

What is a save worth to you?

Your numbers only: this page does not know your save rate and does not promise one. Measure it with the server's /v1/summary.

Subscribers kept per month: - · recurring revenue kept: -

Run it yourself

git clone https://github.com/Duncan-Haywood/fp-monorepo && cd fp-monorepo/ventures/cancel-flow
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=rk_live_... STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_... \
ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) LINK_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 16) \
PUBLIC_URL=https://cancel.example.com COMPANY_NAME=Acme \
node server.mjs          # DRY_RUN=true until you set DRY_RUN=false

# from your app, when a signed-in customer clicks "Cancel subscription":
curl -s -X POST $PUBLIC_URL/v1/links -H "authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" \
  -d '{"subscription":"sub_..."}'    # {"url": ".../c/<signed link>"} -> redirect them

Point a Stripe webhook at /webhook/stripe for customer.subscription.deleted so true churn is recorded. One-click Render deploy and Docker are in the README.

Related tools

Lose customers to failed cards instead? Dunning Engine recovers them, and MRR Pulse shows what churn costs you each month. To see who has already left, run your export through the Stripe Churn Cohort Analyzer; to see who is about to, Churn Radar scores accounts from your own usage events.

Questions

Why not use the Stripe customer portal's cancellation survey?

Stripe's portal can collect a cancellation reason and offer a retention coupon, and for many businesses that is enough. Cancel Flow is for teams that want a different offer per reason (a pause for people who are not using the product, a discount for price objections), a cooldown so nobody farms discounts, and reasons plus save rate in one place you control.

Does it work with annual plans?

Yes. Annual subscribers get a one-time discount on the next renewal instead of a months-long coupon, and monthly equivalents are used for the revenue estimates.

Is it safe to try?

It starts in dry-run mode: the whole flow works and every answer is recorded, but no subscription is changed until you set DRY_RUN=false. Try it with a Stripe test-mode key first.

Can a customer cancel someone else's subscription?

Not through this service. Each link is signed by your server for one subscription, expires (default one hour), and the server checks with Stripe that the subscription belongs to the customer named in the link before changing anything.

Where does my Stripe key live?

In the environment of the server you deploy in your own account. The author runs nothing in between and never sees your key or your customers.

Starting a subscription from a free trial? Trial Converter emails trials with and without a card on file and can extend a card-less trial once, from the same Stripe account.

No warranty. This tool and the server are provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied, and with no uptime or delivery guarantee. They change your customers' subscriptions on your behalf: you are the operator, responsible for your own Stripe account, your terms with customers and the consumer-protection and cancellation rules where they live (some places require cancelling to be as easy as signing up, so keep a plain cancel path). It is not legal, tax, or financial advice. Everything on this page runs in your browser: nothing you enter is uploaded and the page makes no network requests. Usage counters (opt-out below) stay in your browser's local storage.

Sponsor on GitHub ·

render.yaml.text:
# One-click self-deploy: https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>
# Render builds the Dockerfile in YOUR account; nothing runs on the author's.
# It starts in DRY_RUN: set DRY_RUN=false only after you have walked through a test-mode cancellation.
services:
  - type: web
    name: cancel-flow
    runtime: docker
    dockerContext: ventures/cancel-flow
    dockerfilePath: ventures/cancel-flow/Dockerfile
    plan: starter
    healthCheckPath: /healthz
    disk:
      name: state
      mountPath: /data
      sizeGB: 1
    envVars:
      - key: STATE
        value: /data/state.json
      - key: DRY_RUN
        value: "true"
      - key: ADMIN_KEY
        generateValue: true
      - key: LINK_SECRET
        generateValue: true
      - key: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
        sync: false
      - key: STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
        sync: false
      - key: PUBLIC_URL
        sync: false
      - key: COMPANY_NAME
        sync: false
      - key: BRAND_COLOR
        sync: false
      - key: RETURN_URL
        sync: false
      - key: POLICY_JSON
        sync: false
